title: Problems & Complaints
description: Sorting out problems politely: things broken, lost, wrong or late, in shops, hotels and at home.

phrases.japanese: すみません、ちょっと問題があるんですが
phrases.romaji: sumimasen, chotto mondai ga aru n desu ga
phrases.english: Excuse me, there’s a bit of a problem.
phrases.registerNotes: The polite way in. んですが explains, and leaves the sentence open for them to help.

phrases.japanese: お湯が出ないんですが
phrases.romaji: oyu ga denai n desu ga
phrases.registerNotes: A hotel or home problem. ないんですが states it gently; it isn’t an accusation.

phrases.japanese: 隣の部屋がうるさいんですが
phrases.romaji: tonari no heya ga urusai n desu ga
phrases.english: The room next door is noisy.
phrases.registerNotes: Complaining softly at reception. They’ll usually offer to call the room, or to move you.

phrases.japanese: これ、頼んでいないんですが
phrases.romaji: kore, tanonde inai n desu ga
phrases.registerNotes: In a restaurant. Said gently, it’s an easy fix; staff will apologise and take it away.

phrases.japanese: ネットがつながらないんですが

furigana.b: ネットがつながらないんですが

phrases.romaji: netto ga tsunagaranai n desu ga
phrases.registerNotes: つながる is “connect”: phones, the internet, calls. 電話がつながらない — the call won’t go through.

phrases.japanese: 荷物がまだ届いていないんです
phrases.romaji: nimotsu ga mada todoite inai n desu
phrases.registerNotes: For deliveries, or luggage sent ahead. Have the tracking number (お問い合わせ番号) ready.

phrases.japanese: 傷がついていたので、交換してもらえますか
phrases.romaji: kizu ga tsuite ita node, kōkan shite moraemasu ka
phrases.english: It was scratched, so could I swap it?
phrases.registerNotes: Returning something faulty: say what’s wrong, then ask. You’ll need the receipt.

phrases.japanese: 返金してもらえますか
phrases.registerNotes: Japanese shops prefer to swap things (交換); a refund may take a little asking.

phrases.japanese: 責任者の方をお願いできますか
phrases.romaji: sekininsha no kata o onegai dekimasu ka
phrases.english: Could I speak to the person in charge?
phrases.registerNotes: The polite way to escalate. Staff will usually take it seriously; use it only if the first answer doesn’t help.

phrases.japanese: 確認していただけますか
phrases.registerNotes: Asks them to look into it, very politely. Useful for bookings, bills and lost items.

phrases.japanese: 電車に忘れ物をしてしまいました
phrases.romaji: densha ni wasuremono o shite shimaimashita
phrases.english: I left something on the train.
phrases.registerNotes: Tell station staff the line, the time and which carriage. Lost property in Japan very often comes back.
直る is “get fixed”; 直す is “fix (it)”. An illness getting better is 治る.

phrases.japanese: 困っているんですが、助けてもらえませんか
phrases.romaji: komatte iru n desu ga, tasukete moraemasen ka
phrases.english: I’m in a bit of trouble. Could you help me?
phrases.registerNotes: Asking a stranger for help, politely. 困っている (I’m stuck) is less dramatic than 助けて on its own.
